simple_explanation: An account you open with a pension company of your choice. All pension money paid for you goes into it and is invested to pay your benefits at retirement or when your job ends.
source_note: Transfer and RTS items moved to the RSA Transfer entry

simple_explanation: A company licensed by PenCom only to manage pension savings. Some, called Closed PFAs, manage pensions for staff of organisations that had their own pension schemes before the current scheme began in 2004.
source_note: Receiving and Transferring PFA definitions (0046 and 0047) not used

simple_explanation: A company licensed by PenCom to receive pension money from employers and keep it safe for workers, retirees and others entitled to it. It holds the money for the pension company, which manages it.
source_note: Combined all three sources; settling transactions left out for length

simple_explanation: A pension arrangement where both you and your employer pay part of your monthly pay towards your pension at retirement. Its aim is that everyone who worked in Nigeria, including the self-employed, is paid on time.

The law passed by the National Assembly that sets the rules of the Contributory Pension Scheme, so it works the same way across the public and private sectors in Nigeria. The scheme began under a 2004 law, which this 2014 Act replaced.
source_note: Date corrected from PenCom FAQ Q2: CPS established 2004, repealed and re-enacted 2014

simple_explanation: The body set up by the Federal Government to oversee and regulate all pension matters in Nigeria. It licenses all pension companies, issues rules and makes sure pension schemes are run properly.
source_note: Pension operators simplified to pension companies

simple_explanation: A way retirees receive pension from their pension company every month or three months, planned around how long they are expected to live. If they die, the rest goes to those legally entitled to it.
source_note: Mortality tables simplified to how long they are expected to live

simple_explanation: A guaranteed pension for life that a retiree buys from an approved life insurer with their pension savings. If they die within 10 years of it starting, the people they named are paid for the remaining years.
source_note: NAICOM approval detail left out to avoid extra jargon

simple_explanation: A one-time payment from a retiree's pension account at retirement, made after their regular pension amount (paid every month or every three months) has been worked out.
A pension plan that lets self-employed people and those working in organisations with fewer than three employees save towards their pension. There is no fixed minimum amount to pay in.
source_note: 40/60 split (0243) left out because contingent portion is not defined in the pasted sources

simple_explanation: Extra money a worker chooses to pay into their pension account, beyond what is required, through their employer. Part of it can be withdrawn after staying in the account for a minimum period.
source_note: 50% and 2 years left out because source says PenCom may revise them; fcmb_faq-0015 text is cut off mid-sentence

simple_explanation: Your monthly pay as defined in your employment contract. It should be no less than your basic salary plus your housing and transport allowances.
The right to pension and gratuity earned for years worked before the current pension scheme began in June 2004.
source_note: Used the general definition; 0207 is narrower (federal treasury-funded workers only); gratuity is not defined anywhere in the sources

simple_explanation: A life insurance policy an employer keeps for its employees. If an employee dies while still working there, the people they named receive at least three times their total yearly pay.
source_note: Annual Total Emolument simplified to total yearly pay

simple_explanation: Moving your pension account from one pension company to another, handled through a computer system PenCom set up to start, process and track these moves.
A pension scheme where the employer alone carries the full cost of workers' pensions. This differs from the Contributory Pension Scheme, where both employer and worker pay in.
source_note: trustfund_faq-0017 (funded DB accrued benefits) not used

simple_explanation: The person a pension account holder names on their registration form as the contact to reach in an emergency.
